clue.text: Sweet manufacturers with a well-known line

definitions.text: Sweet manufacturers with a well-known line

parts.words: Sweet manufacturers with a well-known line
parts.note: the makers of honey are insects famous for flying straight to a target, the proverbial direct line

explanation.surface: A confectionery firm boasts of a famous product range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet manufacturers' suggests a sweet factory and 'line' a product range; the line is the bee-line, the straight course a bee is said to fly home.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey is a sweet substance made by these insects, and a bee-line is the proverbial straightest route.

clue.text: Star cast for "This is Your Life"-?

definitions.text: Star cast for "This is Your Life"-?

parts.words: Star cast for "This is Your Life"-?
parts.note: a chart cast from the stars claims to tell someone their life, rather than a celebrity cast on a TV show

explanation.surface: A celebrity is chosen to appear on the TV biography show This is Your Life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' and 'cast' suggest a celebrity in a show; an astrologer casts a chart from the stars that says what your life holds.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrological forecast is cast from star positions and claims to describe a person's future.

clue.text: Number of Romans in Christmas Carol 'story

indicators.note: the numeral is placed inside the carol

parts.note: a noel is a Christmas carol
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Romans feature in a Christmas Carol story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christmas Carol' suggests Dickens; it is NOEL, with V placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel is a long fictional story in prose.

clue.text: Like Old Times with Wee Dolly made up so

indicators.note: the letters are made up into a new word

explanation.surface: Nostalgia with a little doll invented to bring back the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' rearranges WEE DOLLY; 'Old Times' are old copies of the newspaper, turned yellow with age.
explanation.definitionFit: Old newsprint turns yellow as it ages.

parts.note: a man's name whose Hebrew meaning is 'stone of help'

explanation.surface: A man seems to be made of stone.
explanation.walkthrough: The name comes from Hebrew 'stone of help', the stone Samuel set up in the Bible; Dickens gave it to Scrooge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew name means 'stone of help', so its bearer is a male named for a rock.

clue.text: Wipes out areas of low growth

definitions.meaning: cancels or removes, as in scrubbing a plan
scrubland, ground covered in stunted bushes

explanation.surface: Something clears away patches of scrubland.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is to cancel it, and scrubland is ground of stunted bushes.

parts.note: the rounded roofs that crown buildings are their heads, and 'dome' is also slang for a person's head

explanation.surface: A question about who leads the architecture department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' looks like people in charge; it means the rounded tops of buildings, and 'dome' is also slang for a skull.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemispherical roofs sit on top of buildings as a head sits on a body.

clue.text: Land's End is now replanned-repudiate this

indicators.note: the end of the word Land's is its last letter
the words are laid out again in a new plan, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cornwall's tip is redeveloped and its people reject the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land's End' looks like the Cornish headland; 'End' takes the last letter of 'Land's', then 'is' stays as written and 'replanned' turns NOW into OWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown is to refuse to acknowledge as one's own, to reject.

clue.text: Oil marred distribution through the post

indicators.note: distributing the letters scatters them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Spilt oil ruined the parcels in the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution' scrambles OIL MARRED; the surface reads it as delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods bought this way are ordered and delivered by mail service.

clue.text: Type of iron, or iron horsepower

definitions.meaning: an iron that uses vapour to press clothes
the power of the old locomotive, the 'iron horse'

explanation.surface: Choosing between a kind of iron and a train's power.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'iron horse' is an old name for a railway engine, driven by vapour power.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes iron can use hot vapour, and old railway engines ran on vapour power.

clue.text: Turn cleric to a way of love .

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a cleric

indicators.note: the word love is to be written a different way, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman is converted to a loving way of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like a command to the cleric; it is the definition, a verb meaning rotate.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolve is to rotate or spin round, as a wheel does.

indicators.note: a confused word has its letters jumbled out of order

parts.note: E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A muddled clergyman finds comfort in being given directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' scrambles PRIEST into RESPIT, then E (east) is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short break from something unpleasant, a period of relief.

definitions.meaning: a ... in old usage is a saving clause or excuse that protects one's reputation

explanation.surface: Gunners fire a volley to preserve their honour.
explanation.walkthrough: Besides a volley of shots, the word (from Latin 'salvo', saving) once meant a reservation or excuse used to save face.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an excuse that rescues pride, the other a burst of artillery fire.

parts.note: drinkers at a pub bar lift their arms to drink and need space on either side to do it

explanation.surface: Weightlifters raising a barbell need somewhere to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar-lifters' suggests weightlifters, but these are drinkers at a pub bar who 'lift the elbow' to drink and need space to do so.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means enough space to move freely, literally room to swing the arm's joint.

definitions.meaning: alert and vigilant, with eyes not shut

explanation.surface: Someone is taken aback yet stays alert.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide eyes show astonishment, and keeping eyes unshut means staying alert to danger.

clue.text: Listen secretly to sound accompaniment of 15's fall

indicators.note: the phrase is to be heard rather than seen, so it is said out loud

parts.note: Eve went with Adam in the Fall, so her drop goes with his

explanation.surface: Listening secretly to the sound of something falling.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is ADAM; his companion in the Fall was Eve, so 'Eve's drop', said out loud, gives the word for listening in.
explanation.definitionFit: Eavesdropping is listening in on others' private talk.

definitions.meaning: Robert ... was a famous Scottish architect of the 18th century
in the Bible the first man created

explanation.surface: Was the architect the first of his kind?
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Adam designed many Georgian houses; in Genesis Adam is the first man.
explanation.definitionFit: A noted Scottish designer of buildings shares his name with the Bible's original man in Eden.

definitions.meaning: one of the guests at the tea party in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: An unhinged merchant joins a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party member' suggests politics; it is the tea party in Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's character is a crazy hat seller who hosts the tea party in Wonderland.

definitions.meaning: in trial matches, a team of Probables plays a team of ...

explanation.surface: A likely rival shows potential.
explanation.walkthrough: British sports selectors hold trial matches between 'Probables', the likely team, and 'Possibles', the challengers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capable of happening has potential, and in trial games the challengers face the likely first choices.

parts.note: a worker who refuses to strike, and also a limb of a dark colour that holds one up

explanation.surface: A support that does not hit anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support' is a leg; a non-striker in a labour dispute is called a strike-breaker with this insulting name.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is an insult for a worker who carries on during a strike.

clue.text: Under-privileged feeling of oriental sea-force suffering a loss

parts.note: E stands for east, the oriental direction

indicators.note: the word for the sea-force loses the letter a, as the clue says

parts.note: a navy is a nation's fighting force at sea

explanation.surface: Hard-up sailors from the East resent their losses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under-privileged feeling' is what the have-nots feel towards those with more; 'suffering a loss' removes the letter A, as the clue spells it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is the resentment those without feel towards people who have more.

indicators.note: organising the letters puts them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Local communists set up a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organization' rearranges LOCAL into COLLA, and 'red' stays as written; in the surface 'red' looks like a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: To be collared is to be grabbed or arrested, taken by the neck.

parts.note: creatures are defined as things that exist, since to be is to exist

explanation.surface: Some things are said to exist merely because they are defined.
explanation.walkthrough: The word itself means 'existing things', so they exist by definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Living creatures are things that have existence.

parts.note: a warning, and the end of a snooker cue coming loose, a likely cause of a bad shot

explanation.surface: A billiards player warns of a probable bad shot.
explanation.walkthrough: A snooker player whose cue's leather tip comes away will miscue; the phrase is also a confidential warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidential warning is a hint given in advance.

parts.note: a fit here is an outburst, and one is said to 'throw' a tantrum or emotional outburst

explanation.surface: Something is suitable to be thrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit for' looks like 'suitable for'; read 'fit' as a noun, an outburst one throws.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit of uncontrolled emotion is something people are said to throw.

definitions.meaning: a type of knot used to fasten a rope

explanation.surface: A knot keeps things suspended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds things up' looks like supporting; it means delaying.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a tying knot and a snag that causes delay.

clue.text: Assassin involved in as public a scandal as any

indicators.note: the name is held within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A killer is caught up in a scandal as big as any.
explanation.walkthrough: Casca was one of the conspirators who stabbed Julius Caesar; the name runs across 'publiC A SCAndal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Casca struck the first blow in the plot that killed Julius Caesar.

parts.note: a newspaper is a ..., and a bed holds linen ones

explanation.surface: Someone reads the newspaper in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper to read' is a newspaper, slang 'sheet'; a bed also has cotton ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is called a sheet, and bed linen consists of them.

clue.text: Hill leads on to the city

indicators.note: the hill comes first, leading the other words in the answer

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A hill path leads on towards the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the city' is a bare definition: the answer is Canada's largest city.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the largest city in Canada, capital of Ontario.

clue.text: "—— of hearts that ever braved the sun" (Browning)

definitions.text: of hearts that ever braved the sun

parts.words: of hearts that ever braved the sun
parts.note: a line of Robert Browning's verse with its first word left blank for the solver to supply

explanation.surface: A line of Victorian poetry with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: Browning's line praises the most daring of hearts that faced the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing superlative describes the most daring and fearless hearts in the poet's line.

definitions.meaning: Anthony Hope, author of The Prisoner of Zenda, gives the possessive of his surname

explanation.surface: A writer called Anthony has ambitions in literature.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Hope was the pen name of the novelist who wrote The Prisoner of Zenda; read as possessive it gives the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist's surname in possessive form matches the plural word for wishes and ambitions.

clue.text: Ship about to enter, hurricane for instance?

indicators.note: the short word for about goes into the aircraft word

parts.note: the Hawker Hurricane was a British fighter plane of the Second World War
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A ship is about to come into port in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hurricane' looks like a storm but is the Hawker Hurricane, a fighter plane; 'to enter' puts RE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a cargo vessel.
